canonical_statement: The review aims to synthesize current evidence on curcumin anti-inflammatory mechanisms, its use across inflammatory diseases, and approaches to improve curcumin pharmacokinetics.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This paper will review the current studies on the anti-inflammatory mechanism of curcumin

canonical_statement: The review reports that curcumin modulates TLR-linked NF-κB, MAPK/AP-1 and JAK/STAT signaling and can inhibit NLRP3 inflammasome activation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Curcumin exerts anti-inflammatory effects by regulating inflammatory signaling pathways

canonical_statement: Across inflammatory cell, animal and clinical reports, the review describes reductions in multiple pro-inflammatory mediators, including IL-1β, IL-6, IL-17, TNF-α, iNOS/NO and MCP-1.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: curcumin decreased levels of pro-inflammatory mediators

canonical_statement: The review describes curcumin as inhibiting Th17 differentiation and supporting Treg/Th17 rebalancing through effects on the IL-23/Th17 axis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Curcumin inhibits Th17 differentiation

canonical_statement: The review links curcumin anti-inflammatory activity to reduced ROS production and Nrf2-Keap1-related antioxidant activity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Curcumin reduces inflammation through its antioxidant activity

canonical_statement: The authors conclude that current evidence suggests curcumin can reduce inflammatory mediators and may benefit IBD, arthritis, psoriasis, depression, atherosclerosis and COVID-19.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: curcumin’s anti-inflammatory properties may have a beneficial effect on these diseases

canonical_statement: For IBD, the authors characterize curcumin as a potentially useful adjuvant, particularly with mesalazine in ulcerative colitis, rather than as an established stand-alone therapeutic agent.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: researchers generally agree that curcumin is used as adjuvant therapy

canonical_statement: The review states that heterogeneous formulation, administration, dose and model-selection standards plus limited bioavailability leave insufficient clinical evidence to establish curcumin as an IBD therapeutic agent.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: there is still no sufficient clinical evidence to prove that curcumin is a therapeutic agent for IBD

canonical_statement: The authors describe clinical trial results in arthritis as promising but conclude that curcumin is not established as an arthritis treatment because available data are limited.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: curcumin is not yet available as a treatment for arthritis due to limited data

canonical_statement: The review notes that clinical evidence for curcumin in psoriasis is low-level and based on small samples.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the level of evidence is low and the sample size is small

canonical_statement: For depression, the review reports inconsistent clinical trial results and calls for larger trials with standardized dose, use and severity-assessment methods.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: clinical trials have not yielded consistent, positive results

canonical_statement: For atherosclerosis, the review identifies a lack of relevant clinical trials and inconsistent clinical findings as reasons for further comprehensive trials.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Due to the lack of relevant clinical trials and inconsistent results

canonical_statement: The review reports early COVID-19 clinical studies in which nano-curcumin or curcumin with piperine was used as adjunctive therapy and was associated with improved recovery-related outcomes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: curcumin with piperine as adjuvant therapy in COVID-19 treatment

canonical_statement: The authors identify low water solubility, poor gastrointestinal absorption, rapid metabolism, elimination and first-pass effects as major pharmacokinetic barriers to curcumin clinical use.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Low water solubility, poor absorption, elimination and rapid metabolism limit the utilization of curcumin

canonical_statement: The review groups proposed countermeasures into curcumin derivatives/prodrugs, pharmaceutical formulation strategies and combination drug therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: current research mainly concentrated in curcumin derivatives and prodrug, pharmaceutical strategies, and combination drug therapy

canonical_statement: The review reports that structural modification, analogues and prodrugs can improve curcumin physicochemical properties and retain or enhance anti-inflammatory activity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: some of which have improved their physicochemical properties and have significant anti-inflammatory effects

canonical_statement: The review describes Theracurmin and other formulation strategies as approaches to improve curcumin solubility, absorption and bioavailability, with reported anti-inflammatory activity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Theracurmin can be dissolved in water, greatly improving the bioavailability

canonical_statement: The review describes combination therapy, including piperine and other bioactive compounds, as a strategy to improve curcumin exposure and anti-inflammatory effects.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: combination therapy is an effective method to improve pharmacokinetics and anti-inflammatory effect of curcumin

canonical_statement: The authors conclude that curcumin dietary supplements or use as an adjuvant are the most feasible application paths described in the review.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: curcumin dietary supplement or adjuvant drug has significant therapeutic effect, which is the most feasible way
